The conflation is the strategy. Game AI was pathfinding and behavior trees, deterministic systems shipped after profiling. Generative slop is statistical content stitched at runtime. Calling both AI lets slop borrow legitimacy from 40 years of engineering.

The conflation is the marketing strategy. 'AI' got rebranded to mean generative output specifically because that's what investors needed to believe was the future. Pathfinding and NPC behavior never threatened a labor market or required an ocean of compute.

The conflation is intentional. Behavior trees and A* are bounded engineered systems. LLM slop is stochastic generation at scale. Bundling them as 'AI' lets the worst use cases hide behind the legitimacy of the older ones.

The conflation does specific work for LLM vendors: it lets every demo claim a 70-year heritage. Pathfinding shipped as a feature. Generative NPC dialogue ships as a beta with a per-token meter attached. Different products, same noun.

Yes. The 'AI' label launders slop alongside genuine capability gains. NPC pathfinding, protein folding, and infinite Studio Ghibli posts are not the same thing. Conflating them helps OpenAI's marketing AND helps angry critics. Both incentives push the same way.

The flattening is the strategy. A* pathfinding and behavior trees have done useful work in games for decades. 'AI-powered' as a label launders that boring credibility into cover for whatever shipped slop the marketing deck needed.

The conflation is doing real work for them. Lumping pathfinding NPCs in with generative slop makes any criticism look like Luddism. Studios shipped ML features for a decade before LLMs without complaint, because the tech served the player and not the marketing deck.

The conflation is the whole strategy. Pathfinding, behavior trees, finite state machines. We had words for these. Calling it all 'AI' lets the slop ride on legitimate decades of work. Branding as a moat.

Right. 'AI' now covers scripted enemy behavior, classical ML like spam filters, generative models, and AGI pitch decks, all under one word. The flattening isn't accidental. It lets a chatbot inherit the goodwill of a Pac Man ghost.

The conflation is the strategy. 'AI' used to mean pathfinding and behavior trees. Investors need it to mean 'thing that scales infinitely with no employees.' Same two letters, completely different deal.

Right. Pathfinding NPCs and generative slop have nothing in common except the marketing department's shared vocabulary. The flattening is the strategy. If everything is AI, criticizing slop sounds like criticizing technology itself.

The conflation is intentional because it makes opposition sound silly. Game AI is hand-authored state machines and pathfinding. Generative models are stochastic remixes of scraped training data. Calling both "AI" is like calling a calculator and a slot machine "math."

Exactly. NPC pathfinding and a chatbot trained on scraped art are not the same animal. The conflation is the marketing trick. 'AI' used to mean a system that solves a defined problem. Now it means generative slop sold by people who own the scrape pipeline.

The slop vs ML distinction also explains why NPC pathfinding never got a billion-dollar valuation. Boring competence doesn't trigger the hype loop. Slop does, because slop scales with compute spend, and that's what investors are actually buying.

Classical game AI is authored behavior. Finite state machines, behavior trees, pathfinding, each output shaped by a designer. The slop problem isn't ML, it's that generative output isn't authored by anyone. The conflation is very much deliberate.

The conflation is the whole business model. Calling slop generators and pathfinding by the same name lets them launder credibility from 40 years of actual ML research. Precision in language is the first line of defense.

The sleight of hand is collapsing two different engineering practices under one label. Pathfinding and behavior trees are authored by humans. Generative models are statistical outputs dressed up as authorship. One is a tool, the other replaces the author.
The conflation is strategic. When 'AI' covers everything from A* pathfinding to hallucinating LLMs, the category becomes useless and every critique loses its target. That's the feature, not the bug.

The conflation is the whole business model. 'AI' meant pathfinding, FSMs, procgen for decades. Now it means whatever the vendor is shipping this quarter. Vague words sell stock better than specific ones.

Worth noting game 'AI' was always a marketing term too. Goomba logic is three lines of code, not intelligence. The word has been strategically slippery for 40 years. What's different now is the output is extractive rather than just entertaining.

The taxonomy collapse is the whole marketing play. Calling a pathfinding algorithm and a diffusion model both "AI" is how they launder 20 years of goodwill from one into the other. Precision in language is resistance.
